I'm a 72-year-old farmer in Quzhou County with a high education level and 50 years of experience, farming 6.5 mu alone in a wheat-maize double cropping system. Let me think through my season.

At my age, with only myself to work the land, I have to be careful. I know the technical recommendations—I've read the extension materials over the years, and I understand the science. But 6.5 mu isn't a business farm; it's barely enough to keep me fed and cover my basic expenses. Every yuan I spend on inputs must be justified. I can't afford to chase maximum yields. I aim for stable, reasonable yields with minimal risk and labor.

**Wheat (6.5 mu, planted early October, harvested mid-June):**
I plant winter wheat on all 6.5 mu. I saved some seed from last year, but I'll buy improved variety seed this year—about 15 kg total for the plot, costing roughly 80 yuan. I know the soil here; it's loam, decent fertility but not rich. I'll apply compound fertilizer as base: roughly 25 kg of a 15-15-15 compound fertilizer per mu (about 3.75 kg N, 3.75 kg P₂O₅, 3.75 kg K₂O per mu), then topdress with urea at jointing—maybe 8-10 kg urea per mu. Total N around 12-13 kg/mu. It's lower than the extension target of 18-20 kg/mu, but at my scale, the marginal return on extra fertilizer doesn't justify the cash outlay. I irrigate three times: once at planting if it's dry, once at wintering if needed, once at jointing, and maybe a light one at grain filling if the spring is dry. I do the irrigating myself; the pump is old but works. For pesticides, I'll spray herbicide once in early spring and watch for aphids—maybe one insecticide spray if I see them. I expect around 420 kg/mu. Last year I got 400 kg/mu; conditions look similar.

**Maize (6.5 mu, planted mid-June right after wheat harvest, harvested late September):**
The turnaround is brutal—sometimes only 3-4 days. I'll hire a combine for wheat harvest (costs about 50 yuan/mu) and then till quickly with my small tiller. I plant hybrid maize seed; I buy it fresh each year, about 2.5 kg/mu, costing around 60 yuan total. Base fertilizer: I apply another round of compound fertilizer, about 20 kg/mu, and that's often it for the season. If the season looks good and I have cash, I might side-dress a little urea at the V6 stage, but honestly, at my age and with labor just me, I often skip it. Total N around 10 kg/mu. Maize here relies on summer rainfall, but if there's a dry spell in July or August, I'll irrigate once or twice. I spray herbicide at pre-emergence and maybe once more if weeds come up. I expect around 480 kg/mu if the weather cooperates.

**Labor and Costs:**
I do all the fieldwork myself except wheat harvest and sometimes maize harvest if my nephew can help. Hired labor is expensive—120-150 yuan per day—and I avoid it. My total input budget is tight: I can spend about 2,800-3,000 yuan for the whole year on both crops. Seeds, fertilizer, pesticide, fuel for irrigation, and combine hire. I don't have much margin for error.

**Tradeoffs:**
I know I could probably push yields to 500 kg/mu for wheat and 550 kg/mu for maize with more fertilizer and irrigation, but that would cost another 800-1,000 yuan in inputs, and on 6.5 mu, the extra revenue doesn't cover the extra cost and labor. At 72, I value stability and my health more than optimization.
